messages.author: 5914e579c97f1326
messages.subject: Type one Interaction in a CAR model
parts:
I am working on a space time CAR model, and wondering which is the right way to specify a type one interaction

either 
f(region.unstruct2,model="iid", group=time.unstruct2,control.group=list(model="iid")

region.unstruct2= unstructured space
time.unstruct2=unstructured time 

 or 

f(ID.Region.Year,model="iid")

where the variable is  the interaction of terms representing unstructured time and  unstructured space

Running either i am getting different posteriors and WAIC

parts:
On Tue, 2018-11-06 at 21:46 -0800, Peter Macharia wrote:
> formulaf<-y ~ 1 + f(region.struct1,model="besag",graph="KEN.adj",
> hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.001))))+
> f(region.unstruct1,model="iid" )+
> f(time.struct1,model="rw1", hyper = list(prec =
> list(prior="pc.prec",param=c(0.33,0.01))))+
> f(time.unstruct1,model="iid")+
> f(ID.Region.Year,model="iid")
> #
> f(region.unstruct2,model="iid", group=time.unstruct2,control.group=li
> st(model="iid")
> modf<-inla(formulaf,family="gaussian", data=data,

You have an confounding effect here with the Gaussian likelihood, since
basically you have like

y_i = \mu + u_i + \epsilon_i

where both u and epsilon are iid Gaussians. So it might happend, due to
paralellism, that the models estimate that most of the variance is
explained by u and less by epsilon, OR, most of the variance by epsilon
and less by u.

You can control this by the prior for u and epsilon, but its a little
``unusual'' setup unless you know well the variance for one of the
effect.

In terms of waic/dic the differences can you huge, for the different
modes.

H




> control.inla=list(diagonal=1e-4),

this argument you do not need.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Type one Interaction in a CAR model
parts:
On Tue, 2018-11-06 at 22:27 -0800, Peter Macharia wrote:
>
> f(region.unstruct2,model="iid",
> group=time.unstruct2,control.group=list(model="iid"). Its it one and
> the same thing or their applications mean different things.
>

this is the same thing. just note that the indexing here is two-
dimensional, so its

c(region.unstruct2[i], time.unstruct2[i])

that is the index for that random effect. as you chose model="iid",
both places, this is an iid effect with this two-dimensional indexing.
